walkthroughs.body_html:
Paper 2: Modern Texts and Poetry — a core area of GCSE English Literature.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Paper 2: Modern Texts and Poetry brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Paper 2: Modern Texts and Poetry.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

Crimean
Napoleonic

mcqs.q: What is the structure of a Shakespearean sonnet?
options: A sonnet must always be exactly ten lines long.
Fourteen lines in iambic pentameter, structured as three quatrains and a final couplet, rhyming ABAB CDCD EFEF GG, often with a volta near the couplet.
A sonnet is any short love poem.
It is a religious text used in Catholic services.

mcqs.q: What is the structural framework of The Canterbury Tales?
options: It is a religious text used in Catholic services.
Postmodernism means writing about the future.
A frame narrative — pilgrims travelling to Canterbury tell stories along the way, allowing Chaucer to juxtapose different voices, genres and social classes.
It is one continuous story told by Chaucer from beginning to end.
Postmodernism means writing about the future.
It is a religious text used in Catholic services.
Self-aware metafiction, intertextuality, scepticism toward grand narratives, playfulness with form, and blurring of high/low culture.
Postmodernism just means literature written after modernism.
